abstract: The addition of haptic feedback as well as visual and audio information can help make live sports broadcasts more immersive. However, it is difficult to add haptic information to the video content in realtime. Thus, we developed a system that analyzes sports videos with low computational cost and displays haptic information depending on the results. The system measures the intensity value of athletes’ motion and the timings of specific actions from input video in realtime. The haptic chair and handheld devices are actuated by the trigger from the video analysis. The system provides viewers with haptic stimuli synchronized with audiovisual information. The haptic stimuli from the devices enhance viewers’ feelings of immersion while watching live sports broadcasts at public viewing events.

authors.bio: Masaki Takahashi received BS and MS degrees in engineering from Keio University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1997 and 1999, respectively, and a PhD degree from the Graduate University of Advanced Studies, Hayama-cho, Kanagawa, Japan, in 2012. He joined Japan Broadcasting Corporation (NHK), Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, in 1999, and he has been working at the Science and Technology Research Laboratories, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo, since 2002. His research interests include visual object tracking and content production technology. He was a visiting researcher at the University of British Columbia, Vancouver, BC, Canada, in 2012.
authors.name: Masaki Takahashi

authors.bio: Taichi Ishiwatari received BE and ME degrees in electrical engineering and bioscience from Waseda University, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo, Japan, in 2015 and 2017, respectively. After his graduation, he joined NHK and has been working at the Science and Technology Research Laboratories since 2019. His research interests include machine learning and natural language processing.
authors.name: Taichi Ishiwatari

authors.bio: Masanori Sano received BE and ME degrees in electronic engineering from Waseda University and a PhD degree in informatics from the Graduate University for Advanced Studies. He joined NHK in 1994, and since 1997 he has been with Science and Technology Research Laboratories. His research interests include information extraction from media, information integration, metadata production system, and universal services. He has been involved with activities at International Telecommunication Union (ITU), Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG), European Broadcasting Union (EBU), Asia-Pacific Broadcasting Union (ABU), and Association of Radio Industries Businesses (ARIB).
authors.name: Masanori Sano
